lineage_context.teaching_goal: Use opposite leaves, many stamens and an inferior-to-half-inferior ovary with capsular fruit to separate the project Philadelphus branch from other Cornales.

project_scope.note: The current pool contains Philadelphus ernestii, P. lewisii and P. texensis. Family recognition is built around Philadelphus; species-level range/taxonomy remains separate.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: On a mock-orange shrub, start with opposite leaves and a white 4-petaled flower. Then look at the center: Philadelphus carries many stamens, usually far more than the petal number, around an inferior to half-inferior 4-locular ovary.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Woody shrubs in the project genus; leaves opposite, simple, usually serrate to entire, without stipules; venation often strongly 3–5-veined from near the base.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers bisexual and radial. In Philadelphus, sepals usually 4, petals 4 and white/cream; stamens commonly 13–90. Hypanthium is adnate to the ovary; ovary inferior to half-inferior, usually 4-locular.
family_diagnostics.fruit: A many-seeded loculicidal capsule with persistent sepals/styles.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Opposite shrub + 4 white petals + a crowded ring of many stamens + inferior/half-inferior ovary = project Hydrangeaceae/Philadelphus.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: opposite node → 4-petal mock-orange flower → many stamens → inferior ovary/hypanthium → capsule → Cornales comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Hydrangeaceae is the many-stamen branch of this Cornales batch. Philadelphus looks simple until you count the stamens and notice where the ovary sits.

steps.title: 1 · Start at the opposite leaf node
steps.look_for: Opposite simple leaves, often with several strong veins rising from near the leaf base.
steps.why_it_matters: Sets up the shrub gestalt but still overlaps Cornus, so flower/fruit confirmation follows.

steps.title: 2 · Count four petals, then many stamens
steps.look_for: Four white petals surrounding a dense ring of many yellow-anthered stamens.
steps.why_it_matters: The high stamen count is a fast project-level split from Cornaceae's 4-stamen flower.

steps.title: 3 · Find the hypanthium/inferior ovary
steps.look_for: The floral cup is adnate to the ovary, placing the ovary inferior to half-inferior beneath the visible flower parts.
steps.why_it_matters: Ovary position links Hydrangeaceae to Cornales while separating it from many opposite-leaved shrubs.

steps.title: 4 · Follow the flower into a capsule
steps.look_for: Dry persistent-sepal capsule with multiple locules and many small seeds.
steps.why_it_matters: Fruit sharply separates Philadelphus from Cornus drupes.

comparisons.title: Hydrangeaceae vs Cornaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can be opposite-leaved shrubs with inferior ovaries. Philadelphus has 4 white petals, many stamens and a dry many-seeded capsule; Cornus typically has 4 stamens and a fleshy drupe.

comparisons.title: Hydrangeaceae vs Loasaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have inferior ovaries and many stamens, but project Hydrangeaceae is a woody opposite-leaved shrub; Loasaceae is usually herbaceous/subshrubby with conspicuous barbed, rough or stinging hairs.

visual_lesson.caveat: Hydrangeaceae is broader than Philadelphus. This project module intentionally teaches the local/project mock-orange door first.

genera.fast_cue: opposite shrub + 4 white petals + many stamens + inferior/half-inferior ovary + capsule

visual_targets.annotation_goal: show attachment of floral cup to ovary
